name: Indegene Ltd
title: Indegene Ltd - 544172 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Indegene Q1 FY27 revenue up 26.5% YoY in USD to $112.5m with EBITDA 16.9%; management reiterates 19–20% margin recovery by Q4 FY27, but this is a services firm with no capacity data and it is a services/pharma commercial business, so the capital-cycle read is thin.

triggers.quote: Through the inflection point in Q3 FY27, the EBITDA in H2 FY27 will be back in the range that we have operated in the past, that is 19% to 20%.

triggers.label: Q1 revenue +6% QoQ, best Q1 in 4 years
triggers.quote: This is the strongest quarter-on-quarter growth we have delivered in a first quarter in four years

triggers.label: DSO up 4 days to 67
triggers.quote: the DSOs, net of unearned and unbilled revenue, was 67 days, up 4 days quarter -on-quarter.

guidance.quote: we expect our organic growth in FY27 to be better than FY26, and we anticipate an acceleration in the second half.

guidance.value: 19% to 20% in H2 FY27; back by Q4 FY27
guidance.quote: It's not going to be 6 to 8, it's going to be 6 . By March end, we get back to that 19% to 20% range.

prior_guidance_check.metric: Margin normalisation in 6–8 quarters from Q3 FY26
prior_guidance_check.quote: we are on track. And the margin normalization is expected in 6 quarters, that is by Q4 of FY27.

themes: Gen AI in pharma commercial ops

red_flags.label: Margin miss vs 6–8 quarter path shifted to 6 quarters; large deal costs front-loaded before revenue
red_flags.quote: the revenue still have to flow in for those deals. And they will flow in, that's what we are talking about, the second half on this year.

red_flags.quote: As a practice, we've been expensing these out.

evasions.quote: We're not breaking up organic and inorganic growth from a BioPharm perspective, anymore.

summary.headline: Indegene Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.7% YoY to INR10,631m, with EBITDA margin at 16.9% and guidance for a return to 19–20% by Q4 FY27.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR10,631 million, up 39.7% YoY in rupee terms and 6% QoQ, with USD revenue of $112.5 million up 26.5% YoY and 2.5% QoQ. Reported EBITDA was INR1,795 million at a 16.9% margin, up 50 bps QoQ against a prior quarter hit by roughly 240 bps of undesignated forex mark-to-market. PAT rose 45.9% QoQ to INR1,162 million (10.9% of revenue). Management reiterated that margins will normalise to the 19–20% band by Q3/Q4 FY27, driven by a large outcome-based omnichannel deal recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 and workforce productivity gains.

financial_highlights.change: +50 bps QoQ reported; prior quarter hit ~240 bps from MTM on undesignated hedges

segments.name: Enterprise Commercial
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 70.6% of revenue in Q1 FY27; segment mix described as stable QoQ.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: 75.1% of revenue; mix described as stable.

segments.name: Accounts beyond top 20
segments.commentary: Contribute 33.4% of total revenue; almost doubled YoY in rupee terms; management says this drove growth.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected back in the 19%–20% range in H2 FY27; management confirmed 19–20% for Q4 FY27 when asked, pulling forward the earlier 6–8 quarter normalisation window (from Oct 2025) to 6 quarters, i.e., by Q4 FY27.
Organic growth in FY27 expected to be better than FY26, with acceleration in H2.
Outcome-based omnichannel engagement (north of $10 million ACV) starts recognising revenue from Q3 FY27; costs already incurred since Q4 FY26, so most revenue expected to drop to bottom line.
Q2 wage hike cycle expected to be offset by workforce transformation savings and Tectonic-related revenue ramp, keeping margins stable rather than declining as in historical Q2.
Undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026; management says hedge accounting adoption removes future MTM volatility from operating margins.
capex_capacity: Management said proprietary tech investment (data layer, Cortex context layer, apps and workflows) has been ratcheted up, but costs continue to be expensed rather than capitalised, though management acknowledged a technical case for capitalisation.
Workforce transformation and Gen AI productivity initiatives across operations and support functions expected to widen progressively.
demand_pricing: Active client count rose 14 QoQ to 105; customers in $10M–$25M bucket increased by 2 to 9; $1M+ clients rose from 36 to 54 over two years (per management, since Q1 FY25).

Q1 deal wins: one $3M–$5M deal with a top-5 customer (content platform migration); four $1M–$3M annual contracts (three commercial, one medical), including Tectonic extension from Germany to Spain; several sub-$1M lead-in deals.
Large Tectonic (Gen AI) engagement in Germany showed measured offtake on existing scope but expanded to Spain.

Outcome-based (pure) contracts are a small part; about 60% of revenue is output-plus-outcome based, with the rest largely hybrid FTE contracts. Hybrid deals typically take 3–4 quarters to ramp to full output revenue.
Renewals run on Jan–Dec cycles; net revenue retention stated above 100%; no major enterprise renewal loss historically.
Industry: top 20 global pharma revenue growing roughly 10%–12% YoY in calendar Q1 2026; immunology, oncology and mental health growing double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a delay to margin normalisation, given Q4 vs H2 wording, and what is the nature of the investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delay: the normalisation is now targeted within 6 quarters from Oct 2025 (by March 2027), not the 6–8 range. Investments were in onsite commercial, medical, consulting and tech staff, plus large strategic deals (Tectonic; a >$1B US brand portfolio physician-outreach contract). Management confirmed this holds despite these deal investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic growth and BioPharm contribution; what was constant-currency growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer splits BioPharm organic vs inorganic; it is now well integrated and both are in the base sequentially. Constant-currency growth was estimated at about 2.6%–2.7% QoQ, versus USD growth of 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of contracts are outcome-based and how does revenue and order book flow?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of contracts are output or outcome based; dedicated FTEs outside this are specialist roles supporting those contracts. Hybrid deals start FTE revenue within a month and ramp output revenue over 3–4 quarters. The large omnichannel deal is pure outcome-based with about 3 quarters of revenue deferral; the client has shared revenue upticks for 5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Gen AI strategy, IP protection, and data ownership concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a layered stack: Indegene data universe at the base, Cortex knowledge layer that is model-agnostic, agent layer (Content Super App, Medical Writing platform), and Transform AI workflows. Management said clients keep data ownership via contract and expect larger pharma to move toward on-prem open-weight models.

qa_highlights.question: What percentage of revenue is AI-led, and what are the margin drivers beyond already-incurred costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify AI-led revenue, saying AI is embedded across all work; content volumes rose 5–7x with falling unit costs. Other margin drivers are growth on fixed GTM and leadership costs and the Tectonic revenue uptick.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 19–20% margin target for Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes for Q4 FY27 when asked directly.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the outcome-based omnichannel deal recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 and on the Tectonic and other large deals ramping; delays would push back the 19–20% target.
Enterprise AI adoption described as measured; Tectonic offtake on existing scope is slow.
Undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026, with residual accounting volatility.
US policy and drug pricing / MFN decisions flagged as the key external watch item; management currently sees the policy outlook as stable.
Receivables: DSO up 4 days to 67; management sees credit risk as minimal, but biotech and emerging-pharma contracts and outcome-based milestones are being monitored.
Q2 wage hike cycle could pressure margin before offsets kick in.
